snip.t: Microthrombi occlude the vessels (the blood supply to the fascia and skin is lost), causing ischaemia, anaesthesia of the skin and necrosis.
Aspiration (the commonest route): alcohol excess, seizures, stroke, reduced consciousness, dysphagia, anaesthesia, poor dental hygiene and gingivitis, GORD.
Also required in practice: informed consent, adequate analgesia/anaesthesia, an empty bladder, appropriate equipment and personnel, and readiness to perform caesarean section if the procedure fails.

qs.q: What is the required duration of fasting for a patient scheduled for general anaesthesia?
o: NPO for at least 4 hours pre-op
NPO for at least 24 hours pre-op
NPO for at least 12 hours pre-op
NPO for at least 30 minutes pre-op
qs.e: To prevent aspiration during general anaesthesia, patients should be NPO for at least 4 hours pre-op. Other durations are either too short to ensure gastric emptying or unnecessarily prolonged.
